title: Eight Men Arrested for Stealing Donations From the Ram Mandir. A Court Is Being Asked to Call In the CBI.
excerpt: CCTV footage, property raids, and a PIL seeking a CAG audit — the embezzlement scandal at Ayodhya's most sacred site is deepening by the day.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Eight men arrested for stealing donations from the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya.
  • Police recovered approximately Rs 80 lakh ($85,000) from the accused.
  • A Public Interest Litigation seeks a CBI investigation and forensic audit of temple finances.
  • Former Trust official claims deeper corruption within temple management.
  • Scandal raises questions about security and accountability at a politically significant site.
The Ram Mandir Scandal Unfolds
January 2024
Ram Mandir consecrated by PM Modi after decades of legal battles.
Recent
Eight men arrested for stealing donations from temple.
Ongoing
SIT investigation and simultaneous raids on accused's properties.
Pending
Allahabad High Court to hear PIL for CBI investigation.
Sources: Reuters, DevDiscourse
The Ram Mandir in Ayodhya was supposed to be beyond reproach. Consecrated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in January 2024 after decades of legal battles, it stands as the most emotionally charged symbol in modern Indian politics — a temple built largely by the donations of millions, including lakhs of NRIs who contributed from abroad. Now eight men have been arrested for systematically stealing from it. An FIR registered under multiple sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita has named all eight: Tinnu Yadav, Anukalp Mishra, Lavkush Mishra, Avinash Shukla, Manish Yadav, Subhash Srivastava, Karunesh Pandey, and Ramshankar Mishra. Most were directly involved in handling, counting, and transporting donations from the temple's collection boxes. Police have so far recovered approximately Rs 80 lakh ($85,000) from the accused, but investigators suspect the actual embezzlement is far larger, stretching back over four years. CCTV footage caught the men siphoning cash from the temple's *hundis* — the brass and wooden donation boxes where devotees drop currency notes and coins. A court has remanded all eight to judicial custody for 14 days. ## The Trail Is Getting Bigger This is not a petty-theft case. An investigative Special Investigation Team (SIT), formed on orders from Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, submitted its preliminary findings to the state government before the FIR was registered. Police are now conducting simultaneous raids on the homes of all eight accused, looking for property deeds, jewellery, and bank records — anything that might explain a sudden shift in the economic status of men who earned modest temple salaries. A Public Interest Litigation (PIL) has been filed in the Allahabad High Court seeking a CBI investigation and a CAG forensic audit of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust's finances. The petition, citing media reports and the fact that temple officials initially denied the allegations, alleges "institutional denial" and questions the Trust's "capacity and willingness to ensure an impartial and effective internal inquiry." Adding explosive detail: Mahipal Singh, the Trust's former Head of Accounts who served from January 2021 to early 2022, has gone public with insider disclosures suggesting the rot runs deeper than the eight arrested staff. Several key individuals in the temple's management have reportedly resigned since the scandal broke. ## Why This Is an Embarrassment for the BJP The political dimension is unavoidable. The Ram Mandir was the BJP's signature achievement — the culmination of a movement that reshaped Indian politics over three decades. The temple's consecration ceremony was broadcast live to hundreds of millions. Modi himself performed the rituals. For the opposition, the scandal is irresistible. Samajwadi Party MLA Ravidas Mahrotra has demanded Yogi Adityanath's resignation, arguing that if the FIR confirms systematic theft "despite so much security and the presence of so many police," the Chief Minister bears moral responsibility.

Adityanath has responded forcefully, saying those involved will "face the consequences." But the damage is less about individual accountability and more about the optics: a temple that symbolised faith, national identity, and political triumph is now in the news for something that looks a lot like a racket. ## What NRIs Should Know For the Indian diaspora, this scandal hits close to home — often literally. Millions of NRIs donated to the Ram Mandir construction fund, many through formal channels set up by the Trust and the VHP. The temple received donations from over 11 crore households across India and abroad. The PIL's demand for a CAG audit is particularly significant for overseas donors. If granted, it would provide the first independent accounting of where the money went — not just the recently embezzled cash, but the entirety of the Trust's finances since its formation. The Allahabad High Court has not yet set a date for hearing the PIL. In the meantime, the SIT investigation continues, and the possibility of more arrests has not been ruled out. For a temple built on the faith of millions, the immediate question is straightforward: how much was taken, and how long did it go on? The harder question — how a site with such intense political, security, and media attention allowed systematic theft for years — may take considerably longer to answer. *Sources: Reuters, DevDiscourse, LatestLY, LiveLaw, LawBeat*
